answer: Each collapsed cluster gets one ember weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. The opal report shows the merge explicitly at each fable. Because of that, an copycat who spins up 300 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 13 times the capital for one share. A farm of 3700 identities would post 3418 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
